title: Final Resolution (Res F) – T-17924 Executive Director Resolution Foresthill U-1009-C AL395 Withdrawal of Service (Final)
text:
Resolution T-17924 Date of Issuance: 7/2/2026
CD/AL6
PUBLIC UTILITIES COMMISSION OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA
Communications Division RESOLUTION T-17924
Carrier Oversight and Programs Branch
R E S O L U T I O N
Resolution T-17924. Approval of Foresthill Co. d.b.a. Sebastian’s (Foresthill) (U-1009-
C) Request for Authority to Withdraw Foreign Exchange Service from its Tariffs.
PROPOSED OUTCOME:
 Approves Foresthill Co. d.b.a. Sebastian’s (Foresthill) (U-1009-C) request
to withdraw Foreign Exchange Service from its tariffs.
SAFETY CONSIDERATIONS:
 There are no adverse safety considerations identified by the
Communications Division. Foreign Exchange Service is a non-essential,
optional add-on service that allows a phone line to receive a number from
a different exchange area. With no connection to emergency services or
essential communications, the removal of Foreign Exchange Service poses
no safety risks.
ESTIMATED COST:
 There are no costs associated with this Resolution.
__________________________________________________________
SUMMARY
This Executive Director Action Resolution authorizes Foresthill Telephone Co. d.b.a.
Sebastian (Foresthill) to withdraw Foreign Exchange Service from Schedule Cal. P.U.C.
No. A-13 and to revise its tariffs to eliminate all corresponding references to the service.
The service is currently grandfathered, and the number of subscribers has steadily
declined. As of 2023, Foresthill has no customers enrolled in the service.
BACKGROUND
610042828

Resolution T-17924
CD/AL6
Resolution T-17020, adopted on April 27, 2006, authorized Foresthill to grandfather its
Foreign Exchange Service offerings to immediate family members residing at existing
premises, prohibiting any moves, additions, or changes to the service. At the time, eleven
customers were subscribed to the service.
On March 17, 2026, Foresthill filed Advice Letter (AL) No. 395 requesting authority to
withdraw Foreign Exchange Service, Schedule Cal. P.U.C. No. A-13, as a tariffed
offering. On April 10, 2026, Foresthill submitted Supplemental AL 395-A (AL 395-A)
reclassifying the Advice Letter as a Tier 3 filing. Pursuant to General Order 96-B
Telecommunications Industry Rule 7.3(7), withdrawal of Foreign Exchange Service
requires a Tier 3 AL filing. Foresthill states that the number of subscribers to the service
steadily declined and that, since 2023, it has no customers utilizing the service.
Foresthill requests the authority to revise its tariffs to withdraw Foreign Exchange
Service from its Schedule Cal. P.U.C. No. A-13 and to eliminate all corresponding
references to the service, including those contained in Schedule A-7, Schedule A-20,
Rules 1 and 2, the Preliminary Statement, and Table of Contents. Foreign Exchange
Service is a classification of exchange service that connects a customer or Private Branch
Exchange (PBX) station to a central office located in a different exchange area from the
customer’s premises. It assigns a phone line a number from a different telephone
exchange area, allowing customers within that exchange area to reach a business or
residence as a local call, regardless of where it is actually located.
NOTICES/PROTESTS
Notice of AL No. 395 was published in the Commission Daily Calendar on March 17,
2026. Notice of AL No. 395-A was published in the Commission Daily Calendar on April
13, 2026. Copies of AL No. 395 and 395-A have been sent to the regular contacts on
Foresthill’s Service List for all advice letter filings.
No protests to this advice letter have been received.
DISCUSSION
In March 1997, through Resolution No. T-9597, the Commission authorized the
Executive Director to grant requests for the withdrawal of communications utility
services for which there are no customers and no requests for such service.
CPUC Communications Division Staff (Staff) reviewed Foresthill’s AL No. 395, as

Resolution T-17924

supplemented by AL No. 395-A, and its associated proposed tariff changes to withdraw
Foreign Exchange Service, and has confirmed that the service has no customers since
June 2023. Foreign Exchange Service is a non-essential, optional add-on service, which
allows a phone line to receive a number from a different exchange area. With no
connection to emergency services or essential communications, the removal of Foreign
Exchange Service poses no safety risks. Staff finds Foresthill’s AL No. 395 as
supplemented by AL 395-A to remove Foreign Exchange Service Offerings and to
eliminate all corresponding references to the service, including those contained in
Schedule A-7, Schedule A-20, Rules 1 and 2, the Preliminary Statement, and Table of
Contents, is reasonable and should be granted.
SAFETY CONSIDERATIONS
Foreign Exchange Service is a non-essential telecommunications service, offering
customers the ability to receive a phone line from a different telephone exchange area,
regardless of their actual location. Its discontinuation poses no risk to public safety or
essential communications.
FINDINGS
1. Resolution T-17020, adopted on April 27, 2006, authorized Foresthill to grandfather
Foreign Exchange Service offerings to immediate family members that reside at
existing premises, prohibiting any moves, additions, or changes to the service.
2. Resolution No. T-9597, dated March 22, 1977, authorizes the Executive Director to
grant requests for the withdrawal of communications utility services for which there
are no customers and no requests for such service.
3. On March 17, 2026, Foresthill filed AL No. 395, and subsequently submitted
Supplemental AL 395-A reclassifying the advice letter as a Tier 3 filing, to withdraw
Foreign Exchange Service because there are no customers nor demand for the
service, and to eliminate all corresponding references to the service, including
those contained in Schedule A-7, Schedule A-20, Rules 1 and 2, the Preliminary
Statement, and Table of Contents.
4. Foreign Exchange Service is a classification of exchange service that connects a
customer or PBX station to a central office in a different exchange area than where
3

Resolution T-17924

the station is located.
5. Staff have reviewed Foresthill’s AL No. 395 as supplemented by AL No. 395-A and
its associated proposed tariff changes to withdraw Foreign Exchange Service.
Staff confirms that the service has no customers nor is there any demand for the
service since 2023.
6. In accordance with the authority granted to the Executive Director pursuant to
Resolution No. T-9597, Foresthill’s AL No. 395 as supplemented by AL 395-A to
remove Foreign Exchange Service Offerings and to eliminate all corresponding
references to the service, including those contained in Schedule A-7, Schedule A-20,
Rules 1 and 2, the Preliminary Statement, and Table of Contents, is reasonable and
should be granted.
THEREFORE, IT IS ORDERED that:
1. Foresthill Telephone Co. d.b.a. Sebastian is granted authority to withdraw Foreign
Exchange Service from its Schedule Cal. P.U.C. No. A-13 and to eliminate all
corresponding references to the service, including those contained in Schedule A-7,
Schedule A-20, Rules 1 and 2, the Preliminary Statement, and Table of Contents, as
filed in Advice Letter No. 395 as supplemented by Advice Letter 395-A.
This Resolution is effective today.
I hereby certify that this Resolution was adopted by Executive Action Resolution on
July 1, 2026.
